hero.title: Some Applications of Plasma
hero.lead: From display screens to nuclear fusion, and from coating spacecraft to breaking up kidney stones: plasma has nine important application areas in our lives, industry, and medicine.

objectives: States the nine applications of plasma in industry, medicine, and space.
Distinguishes between the working principle of a neon lamp and a fluorescent lamp.
Explains the importance of nuclear fusion energy (plasma energy) as a future energy source.

content.heading: 💡 6-9 Some Applications of Plasma
content.html: Plasma has many applications in various fields of life, industry, medicine, and space. Among the most important are:

content.label: 🔢 Enumeration — Applications of Plasma
listItems: 2- Plasma in lamps, where there are two types of lamps that rely on plasma as their source: the first is the neon lamp, and the second is the fluorescent lamp.

4- Plasma coating, which helps reduce the effect of high temperatures on the surfaces of vehicles, especially aircraft; plasma is sprayed by a robot at high temperatures to form the thermal insulation layers of spacecraft, aircraft, and engines.
5- Treating household and industrial waste by separating its constituent elements.
6- Some spacecraft and artificial satellites use plasma thrusters for movement in space or to adjust their position.

7- Medical applications: the waves generated from plasma are used in breaking up kidney stones by means of a shock-wave device, manufacturing medical ceramics, medical sterilization, and other medical applications.
8- Plasma is a good chemical agent for cleaning surfaces, and is also used in chemical analysis.
9- Electric arcs in welding, cutting, and machining metals, etc.

content.sectionHeading: 🕹️ Interactive Simulation: Neon Lamp vs. Fluorescent Lamp
content.descriptionHtml: Choose a lamp type to see the difference in its working principle and the color of the glow produced by the plasma inside it.

labels.neonCaption: Neon lamp: ionized neon gas (plasma) glows directly with a distinctive orange-red color when an electrical voltage is applied across the ends of the tube.
labels.fluorGlowLabel: Converts ultraviolet light into white light
labels.fluorCaption: Fluorescent lamp: mercury vapor atoms become ionized and emit ultraviolet light, which an internal phosphor coating absorbs and converts into visible white light.

content.html: Focused laser beams can be used to produce plasma at extremely high plasma temperatures inside a laboratory at low cost, and this system has many applications in the field of astrophysics.

The most common energy sources today are (coal and petroleum), and global demand for them is growing; these sources are expected to be unable to meet this demand by around the middle of this twenty-first century. This makes clear the need for a clean, safe source that lasts a long time, and perhaps one of the most important of these sources is (plasma energy), whose source is (nuclear fusion energy).

summary.heading: 📋 Lesson Summary
items: Applications of plasma: display screens, lamps (neon/fluorescent), nuclear fusion, thermal coating for aircraft and spacecraft.
Waste treatment, spacecraft propulsion, medical applications (breaking up stones, medical ceramics, sterilization), chemical cleaning, electric-arc welding.
Plasma can be produced in the laboratory with focused laser beams at low cost, with applications in astrophysics.
Plasma energy (nuclear fusion) is a candidate to become the clean energy source that replaces coal and petroleum in the future.
